security_audit.summary: Most alerts are false positives from Markdown fences, quoted substitutions, documentation URLs, and relative links. Six static findings remain for shared temporary files and persisted release credentials. Additional risks include mutable package execution, untrusted metadata entering AI generation, and emergency gate bypasses.

remediation.issue: Mutable claude-flow@alpha packages execute during privileged release steps.
remediation.suggestion: Pin an audited version and integrity through the lockfile, invoke the local binary, and isolate generation from publishing credentials.

remediation.issue: The npm token is written to repository-root .npmrc before a Docker build.
remediation.suggestion: Use step-scoped NODE_AUTH_TOKEN, remove .npmrc immediately after publishing, and exclude credential files from every Docker build context.

remediation.issue: GitHub authentication is persisted before third-party package execution.
remediation.suggestion: Provide GH_TOKEN only to required steps, avoid gh auth login in CI, and reduce workflow permissions to each operation.

remediation.issue: Release metadata uses predictable shared temporary paths.
remediation.suggestion: Create private files with mktemp, restrict permissions, verify ownership, and remove them with a trap after use.

remediation.issue: Repository-controlled text enters AI changelog generation.
remediation.suggestion: Treat PR and commit text as untrusted data, delimit it clearly, disable tool execution, and require human review before publication.

remediation.issue: Emergency examples bypass normal release validation.
remediation.suggestion: Keep mandatory security and smoke tests, require protected-environment approval, and limit fast-track activation to authorized maintainers.

content.user_title: Automate GitHub Releases with Coordinated Workflows
content.value_statement: Manual releases can miss version, validation, artifact, and communication steps. This skill guides release planning, testing, publishing, deployment, monitoring, and rollback with reusable workflows.
actual_capabilities: Drafts GitHub CLI workflows for tags, release notes, pull requests, and artifact uploads.
Coordinates version suggestions, changelog generation, builds, tests, security checks, and publishing steps.
Provides GitHub Actions examples for standard releases and issue-triggered hotfixes.
Describes staged deployments, multi-repository releases, monitoring, and rollback triggers.
Covers npm packages, Docker images, GitHub releases, and binary artifacts.
Provides structured pre-release, release, and post-release checklists.
limitations: The skill provides guidance and examples, not a bundled release executable.
GitHub CLI, Node.js, npm, Docker, Claude Flow, and authenticated services may be required.
Repository names, versions, permissions, environments, and approval rules require project-specific changes.
Claude Flow subcommands and flags must be verified against the installed version.

use_cases.title: Prepare a routine package release
use_cases.description: A maintainer plans a semantic version, validates changes, drafts notes, publishes artifacts, and completes post-release checks.

use_cases.title: Standardize an organization release
use_cases.description: A release manager converts existing controls into a staged GitHub workflow with approvals, monitoring, announcements, and rollback criteria.

use_cases.title: Coordinate dependent repositories
use_cases.description: A DevOps engineer sequences compatible versions across services, validates integrations, and defines an atomic rollback plan.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a patch release
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a patch release for [repository] from [current version]. List prerequisites, validation steps, GitHub release actions, and a rollback checkpoint.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning for a single repository

prompt_templates.title: Draft reviewed release notes
prompt_templates.prompt: Create release notes for [version] from these approved changes: [changes]. Group features, fixes, breaking changes, upgrade steps, contributors, and known issues.
prompt_templates.scenario: Preparing clear notes from reviewed changes

prompt_templates.title: Design a protected release workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a GitHub Actions workflow for [project]. Include least-privilege permissions, pinned dependencies, tests, artifact signing, approvals, publishing, monitoring, and credential cleanup.
prompt_templates.scenario: Building a controlled continuous delivery workflow

prompt_templates.title: Coordinate a multi-repository release
prompt_templates.prompt: Coordinate releases for [repositories and versions] with [dependencies]. Define sequencing, compatibility gates, staged deployment, observability, failure handling, atomic rollback, and communications.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced release coordination across dependent systems

output_examples.input: Plan a patch release from version 2.4.0 for three approved fixes.
output: Recommended version: 2.4.1, pending review of the approved fixes.
Pre-release: verify main, run tests, scan dependencies, and draft notes.
Release: create a protected tag, publish signed artifacts, and retain manual deployment approval.
Post-release: validate health metrics, announce availability, and retain rollback target 2.4.0.

output_examples.input: Create release notes for version 3.0.0 with one breaking API change.
output: Release 3.0.0 introduces the new account API and removes the deprecated profile endpoint.
Migration required: update profile requests before deployment and verify client compatibility.
Known limitation: legacy clients require the compatibility adapter during transition.

output_examples.input: Review a proposed GitHub Actions release workflow for operational risk.
output: Blocker: the npm token remains in a repository file during the Docker build.
High priority: replace mutable package versions and reduce job permissions.
Required gate: keep human approval before production publishing and verify rollback readiness.

best_practices: Verify installed commands, supported flags, and exact dependency versions before running a release.
Create draft releases first, preserve protected approvals, and review generated notes before publication.
Use least-privilege permissions, step-scoped secrets, private temporary files, and explicit credential cleanup.
anti_patterns: Do not execute mutable prerelease packages inside jobs holding repository or registry credentials.
Do not publish from unreviewed branches or bypass required validation because a release is urgent.
Do not write credentials into repository files or release data into predictable shared temporary paths.

faq.question: Does this skill execute releases automatically?
faq.answer: It provides commands, workflow examples, and coordination guidance. Execution depends on the connected tools, credentials, and user approvals.

faq.question: Which access is required?
faq.answer: Required access depends on the workflow. GitHub releases need repository permissions, while package and container publishing need separate scoped credentials.

faq.question: Which project types are supported?
faq.answer: The examples emphasize Node.js packages, Docker images, binaries, monorepos, and multiple repositories. Other projects require adapted build and publishing steps.

faq.question: How should credentials be protected?
faq.answer: Use step-scoped environment variables, least-privilege tokens, protected environments, secret masking, private temporary files, and immediate cleanup.

faq.question: Can the guidance work without Claude Flow?
faq.answer: Core GitHub CLI and checklist guidance can be adapted independently. Swarm coordination and Claude Flow subcommands require the external package.

faq.question: Does this replace release review?
faq.answer: No. Review version decisions, generated notes, security results, artifacts, approvals, deployment health, and rollback readiness before publication.
